## ZScaler Client Connector on Linux and systemd-resolved

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnBlCAI/zscaler-client-connector-on-linux-and-systemdresolved
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-05-31T08:47:21.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

Virtually_Nick

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

August 21, 2021 at 7:52 PM

ZScaler Client Connector on Linux and systemd-resolved

I’m using ZScaler Client Connection on Fedora Core 33, which has switched from the traditional /etc/resolve.conf configuration to using systemd-resolved. With this install, the DNS configuration for ZPA does not get updated properly, and I have to manually use “resolvectl�? on Linux to set the domain name and DNS server for ZPA to work properly.

Is there any configuration that can be done to make this work properly, or any way to file a feature request to get systemd-resolved support added to ZCC for Linux?

Client Connector

1 answer

1.29K views

fvdnabee

(Customer)

5 years ago

I agree ZSS’ support for systemd-resolved could be improved, there are (at least) four options:

ZSS could maintain a systemd-resolved config file in /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/

ZSS could use

resolveconf

. On Arch systemd-resolved supports this via systemd-resolvconf.

ZSS could call resolvectl to configure the DNS servers.

If the system also uses systemd-networkd, then the DNS settings could be configured as a /etc/systemd/network/*.network file

Any other methods?

Currently I know two ways to get ZSS to work with systemd-resolved:

call resolvectl manually as OP pointed out

Don’t symlink /etc/resolv.conf, then systemd-resolved will use /etc/resolv.conf as an input as mentioned

here

I’m using the latter option, though I notice systemd starts off with the internal DNS but then switches to my ISP’s DNS server; which makes internal hostnames unresolvable. Haven’t been able to figure out a good work-around for this so far, apart from calling

systemctl restart systemd-resolved

My setup with /etc/resolve.conf as a file:

? cat /etc/resolv.conf

nameserver 100.64.0.2

nameserver 127.0.0.53

nameserver 195.130.130.2

nameserver 195.130.131.2

search reno.local group.mycompany.com apac.group.mycompany.com nasa.group.mycompany.com emea.group.mycompany.com mycompany.group home telenet.be

? resolvectl status

Global

Protocols: +LLMNR +mDNS -DNSOverTLS DNSSEC=no/unsupported

resolv.conf mode: foreign

Current DNS Server: 195.130.130.2

DNS Servers: 100.64.0.2 195.130.130.2 195.130.131.2

Fallback DNS Servers: 1.1.1.1 9.9.9.10 8.8.8.8 2606:4700:4700::1111 2620:fe::10 2001:4860:4860::8888

Note how systemd-resolved switched to 195.130.130.2 (my ISP’s DNS server, coming in over DHCP). Not sure what triggered the switch.

Hi,

For tunnel 2.0, you need to also add a pac file in your forwarding profile and leverage a specific bypass variable, before web traffic can be bypassed. The app profile pac file is still required, but it won’t work without the other pac file:

https://help.zscaler.com/z-app/best-practices-adding-bypasses-z-tunnel-2.0

Best Regards,

katlyn.gallo

Katlyn Gallo

August 20 |

| - |

I actually just got it working! It seems there were two issues that were contributing to the problem:

wildcard character was not working (ex. *.

google.com

the order of operations was not correct in our forwarding profile pac. The default operation of return “direct? was before the bypassing I was attempting to do.

Here are the final exclusions that are working correctly now.

App profile pac:

/* China Hospital site added Aug 9, 2021 by KG */

if (dnsDomainIs(host, “

fuwu.most.gov.cn

?)) return “DIRECT?;

Forwarding profile pac:

function FindProxyForURL(url, host) {

/* China Hospital site added Aug 9, 2021 by KG */

if (dnsDomainIs(host, “

fuwu.most.gov.cn

?)) return “PROXY ${ZAPP_TUNNEL2_BYPASS}?;

/* Default Traffic Forwarding, Return DIRECT to tunnel using Tunnel2 */

return "DIRECT";

## Azure private DNS and azure zscaler connector

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnD3CAI/azure-private-dns-and-azure-zscaler-connector
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-07-06T13:04:07.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

john.duffield

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

August 20, 2021 at 10:51 AM

Azure private DNS and azure zscaler connector

Hi all Has anyone used Azure private DNS for the azure zscaler connector , is this feasible and what design options are there?

This scenario is to access vms ( rdp and ssh) in a vnet in azure via ZPA with no other connectivity to the subscription to our network.

We would like to use DNS to add the application segment . Can you use IP ranges instead?

Client Connector

1 answer

778 views

john.duffield

(Customer)

Edited by sfdc July 6, 2023 at 12:05 PM

Ok solved this myself Installed ZPA connector on vnet1 in azure with a public ip and setup in zpa cloud using provisioning key .

Add private DNS Zone in azure e.g.

joebloggs.com

, add a vnet link to vnet1 in the Private DNS zone , ensuring auto-registration is ticked. A newVM using vnet1 will register as

newVM.joeblogs.com

Add application segment rule in zpa , points to zpa connector and uses *.joebloggs.com as a catch-all in the rule .

So you can get your DEV people accessing/testing VMs, webapps etc without needing public ip addresses. I setup RDP HTTPS and SSH to *.joebloggs.com. Note with vnet peering we can add as many vnets as needed across multiple subscriptions.

Hi, pls see this document :

Best Practices for Adding Bypasses for Z-Tunnel 2.0 | Zscaler

Use the forwarding profile and APP profile PAC files.

Forwarding profile :

function FindProxyForURL(url, host) {

if (dnsDomainIs(host, “?))

return “PROXY ${ZAPP_TUNNEL2_BYPASS}?;

/* Default Traffic Forwarding. Return DIRECT to tunnel using Tunnel2 */

APP profile:

function FindProxyForURL(url, host) {

/* Updates are directly accessible */

if (dnsDomainIs(host, “?))

return “proxyIP:port?;

/* Default Traffic Forwarding */

return “PROXY ${GATEWAY}:443?;

## ZAPP Connector on AWS Transit Gateway

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnD7CAI/zapp-connector-on-aws-transit-gateway
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-05-31T08:47:24.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

Manoj07

(Partner) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

August 17, 2021 at 11:13 AM

ZAPP Connector on AWS Transit Gateway

Hello Team,

We want to Deploy APP Connectors on AWS to reach AWS resources/workloads.

We do have 30+ AWS accounts, with NO VPC Peering enabled between the accounts.

I have read about deploying APP Connector on Transit Gateways.

But how the Connectivity should be Made and how all the applications can be reachable.

Is the connector must be placed on the transit Gateway or Near the Load balancer.

Can you Please give some inputs on this.

Manoj

Client Connector

1 answer

361 views

Pat_Nicholson

(Employee)

5 years ago

The App Connector needs access to the apps or resources you’d like it to provide to users (internal), so place it in the environment where it can reach all of your assets. It’s best to ensure there are no FWs in between the App Connector and the app or resource unless you are willing to maintain those rules. Also, the App Connector just needs outbound 443 in order to reach the ZPA cloud. I typically suggest to place the App Connector where it has the most access to what your ZPA users need (apps, servers, resources). That will be a bigger challenge than enabling outbound 443 access for the App Connector.

likes this.

Mac1809

(Partner)

5 years ago

Thanks Raj for your comment!!!

And one more thing if you can help me …what is the exact difference between these two action (Enforce & Apply on network changes) for Configure System proxy setting option in forwarding profile .

The given explanation is as follows

Enforce: Client Connector enforces your proxy settings by monitoring for network changes and reapplying setting

Apply on Network Changes: Client Connector only enforces your proxy settings when the network changes, it does not monitor for proxy change afterward;

rajk5

(Employee)

Edited by sfdc July 6, 2023 at 12:06 PM

@Mac1809

When the app detects “trusted Network? based on the criteria you have configured in forwarding profile, you can go with one of the following options:

image

789×112 7.6 KB

Tunnel: Even though you are on a trusted network, all your port 80 and 443 traffic will still be tunneled through Zscaler client connector (ZApp) using it own Z tunnel with an HTTP connect header.

Tunnel with Local Proxy: Though you are connected to a trusted network, Zscaler client connector will install a pac file on your device so that all traffic is tunneled to Zscaler through local host.

Enforce Proxy: Traffic will not be tunneled, instead system proxy settings will be used. You can also push proxy settings via ZCC while using “enforce proxy? option.

None: On detection of trusted network, Zscaler client connector “turns off? and does nothing. “On trusted network? message is displayed. All traffic is sent direct.

Hope this information helps you out!

Internet Bandwidth issue

Hello,

We have been noticing that Internet Speed of some end-users is reducing drastically post installing Zscaler Client Connectors.

If the ISP speed is 100 MBPS, user is getting just around 2-5 MBPS when performing a speedtest.

If we remove the ZCC from the system, then again Internet speed is normal (80-100 MBPS).

Rahul V

likes this.

User16500487481361745088

(Customer)

4 years ago

I just figured this same problem out. It ended up being the windows filtering platform dropping traffic due to the network isolation policy. It’s let of windows defender but the filter still drops traffic on the loop back interface. You can verify with a netsh debug then look inside the net events.xml you will see the drops. Add a GPO for defined subnets and it will fix it.

https://thewindowsupdate.com/2021/07/02/diagnosing-network-isolation-issues/amp/

PAC logic for Wildcard Bypass for ZCC

If you want a wildcard to bypass traffic from ZCC using a wildcard there are a few interesting situations.

Using the following guide to help create App profile PAC and Forwarding profile PAC:

Best Practices for Adding Bypasses for Z-Tunnel 2.0 | Zscaler

If you use “(dnsDomainIs(host, “�?))�?. To create a wildcard you have to use the “.�? not “*�?.

Ie “ (dnsDomainIs(host, “.zscaler.com�?) will capture all subdomains. But if you did “*.zscaler.com�? if it wouldn’t work.

HOWEVER!

If you use “(shExpMatch(host,"")�?, then you have to use “*�? and NOT “.�?.

Ie “(shExpMatch(host,"*.zscaler.com")�? will capture all subdomains, and “.zscaler.com�? would not!

Hope this helps.

July 6, 2021 at 4:15 PM

Cloud FW controls not applying to ZApp connections from a defined network location?

Has anyone run into this? All our machines have ZApp installed, they connect from defined locations (i.e. NOT road warrior) and the location has FW enabled, however the FW rules are apparently completely being ignored. These machines connect using Tunnel 2.0 (I’ve tried both TLS and DTLS flavors) As an aside I also maintain IPSec tunnels for a different internal network location to the ZIA edge.

For example I have a rule defined to block TCP/4099 outbound. On machines riding the IPSec tunnel to ZIA I go to portquiz and test 4099, sure enough the traffic is blocked. An endpoint machine, in a different subnet defined as a different network location, I try the same test and get right out via TCP/4099. I’ve tried numerous other ports and the behavior stays the same. For my machines with ZApp installed the FW only seems to apply when the machines are in the ‘road warriors’ location.

I’ve done the whole packet capture thing and the outbound traffic IS being tunneled through to ZIA, its just not being filtered.

Joe,

If you want to send your DNS traffic to Zscaler via Ztunnel 2.0, you can do so by Entering * in the Domain Inclusions in App Profile and put it any required Domain Exclusions.

As Domain Exclusion for DNS Requests you probably want to add internal domains and any external domains you want to resolve locally… (eg.

and

If you have found the answer, I hope you let us know here on the Community.

If we bypass ZTunnel 2 for DNS requests then we cannot enforce the DNS policy in Zscaler?

Marco_Put-Carstens

(Employee)

5 years ago

I assume you have configured 8.8.8.8 as your primary DNS server. ZCC needs to bypass DNS server in order to be able to do local DNS requests.

When on-trusted network these normally are your internal DNS servers. When user is on home network or some public WIFI, the network DHCP server might be configured to use the Google DNS (8.8.8.8/8.8.4.4.).

The configured DNS server need to be automatically bypassed from ZTunnel 2, as your device needs to be able to resolve the Zscaler services (PAC files, Zscaler nodes, and any local services).

Does this answer your question?

## Directing Microsoft Office 365 (O365) Login Traffic

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnEMCAY/directing-microsoft-office-365-o365-login-traffic
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-07-07T11:21:26.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

Kris_Hubert

(Employee) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

Edited by sfdc July 7, 2023 at 11:21 AM

Directing Microsoft Office 365 (O365) Login Traffic

DRAFT IN PROGRESS!

Background:

I’ve been working with a current customer to roll out Z-App, and migrate away from a PAC file using a Dedicated Proxy Port (DPP). In order to do this, we started with a clean default PAC file.

Their previous PAC file had many (but not all) of the O365 URLs completely bypassing Zscaler. They did this so that they bypass multi-factor authentication when users logged into O365 from a corporate location. Unfortunately, this also meant that they lost visibility to this traffic and they didn’t benefit from Zscaler’s technical relationship with Microsoft.

The customer was also having some authentication challenges, and the customer has now decided to leave Z-App enabled for on-premises and off-premises users.

First Use-Case:

Since the authentication process is the only time Microsoft applies conditional access policies related to source IP address, you don’t need to bypass Zscaler for all of the traffic. You only need to carve off the login traffic from Zscaler.

To do this, we added the below lines to the default PAC file, and applied it to an Z-App Profile.

if (localHostOrDomainIs(host, “ANY_IDP_URL??)) ||

(localHostOrDomainIs(host, “

login.microsoft.com

??")) ||

(localHostOrDomainIs(host, “

login.microsoftonline.com

??)) ||

(localHostOrDomainIs(host, “

login.windows.net

??)) ||

(localHostOrDomainIs(host, “

login.office365.com

??))

return “DIRECT??;

Doing the above will send only this traffic direct.

If the user is on-premises, the traffic will egress with the customer’s IP address. This IP address is whitelisted within the conditional access, and the user will not be prompted for MFA.

If the user is off-premises, the traffic will egress with the end user’s IP address… prompting for multi-factor authentication (MFA).

Another use case is if the customer also has ZPA, and they want to lock down their Office365 traffic to their corporate egress IP addresses.

The same concept above applies here. Except this time, we use ZPA to direct just the login traffic to one more more ZPA Connector Group.

To accomplish this, create an App Segment for the login URLs.

Screen Shot 2020-03-31 at 11.56.38 AM

2126×462 45.1 KB

This will force just the login traffic over ZPA, and to reach the appropriate URLs from the customer’s egress IP addresses that have been whitelisted with Microsoft’s conditional access.

sumanthdandaboina

(Customer)

6 years ago

Found solution,

You have to add your Client email account under “email & app accounts? which will resolve the issue. Once you add client account there, it will start prompting to select which account to use everywhere where ever Azure authentication is present.

Note: This option to add client email account is only available from OS Build version 1809 & 1909 versions.

Selected as Best

After many attempts I managed to fix it in the following way:

I have logged out of portal-office

I logged out of the Edge Microsoft synchronized account

I logged back into Edge using the account I want to use on Zscaler

I have reconnected to portal-office using the account I want to use on Zscaler

Restarted Zscaler and it finally allowed me to choose the account

Hi all,

We have recently enabled SCIM, we now want to enable ZPA for selected groups, but our AD groups have not yet appeared in the “

mobile.zscloud.net

�? portal under “Zscaler Service Entitlement�?

How long do we need to wait for these groups to populate?

amir03

Edited by sfdc July 6, 2023 at 12:04 PM

amayor:

The ZIA portal syncs with the mobile portal every 6 hours by default. If your AD groups are already synced through SCIM on your ZIA admin portal then you can run this sync manually as well . Please go through the following KB article for more information on the manual sync.

Thanks for your quick response…!!

amayor

(Employee)

5 years ago

Hi Amir,

Users can be provisioned on the ZIA portal via the following options:

1)SCIM

2)SAML Auto-provisioning

3)AD sync or ZAB sync

4)CSV Upload

5)Manual creation of users

Irrespective of the method used, the ZIA user database synchronizes with the ZCC database every 6 hours. To answer your question, the sync manual option would work with any provisioning method and is not only limited to SCIM.

Hope this helps!

Regards

Ajar Mayor

The ZIA portal syncs with the mobile portal every 6 hours by default. If your AD groups are already synced through SCIM on your ZIA admin portal then you can run this sync manually as well . Please go through the following KB article for more information on the manual sync.

https://help.zscaler.com/z-app/syncing-directory-groups-between-zscaler-admin-portal-and-app-portal

Hope this helps!

## Zapp Trafic forwarding Port 8080

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnF5CAI/zapp-trafic-forwarding-port-8080
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-07-07T11:30:48.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

yosr

(Partner) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

June 13, 2019 at 1:27 PM

Zapp Trafic forwarding Port 8080

hello,

We have a problem with the port through which pass the flows.

Indeed we opened the flows to 80 and 443 on the firewall, but we notice that the flows pass through port 8080.

We looked at the logs and on wireshark to check which port the flows are going through and we found that this is port 8080.

Anyone have a solution to this problem ?

Client Connector

6 answers

1.31K views

mgorman

(Employee)

5 years ago

Team,

Just a friendly update to this Article:

The forwarding behavior of the Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC; formerly Z-App) described here, wherein it first tries to connect to Port 443, then Port 80, and finally to Port 8080, is ONLY for Tunnel 1.0 (all forms, including TWLP)

For

Tunnel 2.0

(used to send all Ports & Protocols to ZIA), the ZCC will only use UDP or TCP port 443 (depending on Configuration, including Fallback behavior)

Regards,

MJG

dcreedy

(Employee)

7 years ago

Nick is correct, Z App will attempt to connect on 443, if this is blocked it will try 80, and then if this is blocked finally it will try 8080.

I’d say in this case, Z App isn’t able to connect on 443 or 80 and this is causing it to try 8080.

Regards

David

1 like

racingmonk

(Employee)

7 years ago

I think

@Lmay

is probably correct in that 80 or 443 is probably blocked somewhere still. ZApp will only forward on 8080 if 80 / 443 are blocked.

https://ips.zscloud.net/zscaler_app

Modifying the port in the App PAC file will not alter the port the ZApp tunnel uses.

fraya

Hi Jitumani,

I have seen this behaviour. Usually it has been because the user doesn’t exist in the Zscaler user database or has been deleted, if you are using SAML perhaps auto-provisioning isn’t working correctly for this user or the client can’t see your SAML IdP. Its always worth logging out of Zapp and logging back in (using the logout button, not just rebooting the machine) to generate a new SAML assertion.

thanks

Alex

## How to listen the traffic which works on customized ports (other than 80 & 443)?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009eykLECAY/how-to-listen-the-traffic-which-works-on-customized-ports-other-than-80-443
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-11-27T18:44:17.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

subham.ghorui

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

May 28, 2023 at 3:24 PM

How to listen the traffic which works on customized ports (other than 80 & 443)?

As of now all the traffic which works port 80 & 443 is going through zscaler and other than these ports I have to bypass those URL through PAC & doing the provision directly on firewall. Is this the best practice? Is there anything to do in zscaler so that all the web traffic which works on customized ports will go through zscaler?

ZIA - Forwarding

6 answers

1.6K views

Top Rated Answers

Choon_Ping_Koay

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hi Subham,

I am assuming you are referring to using ZCC as the method to forward the traffic to Zscaler. If yes, I believe you have deployed Z-Tunnel 1.0 which supports forwarding port 80/443 traffic to Zscaler cloud. In order to support forwarding all ports and protocols, you may need to open a support case to enable Z-Tunnel2.0 in your tenant and change the tunnel mode to Z-Tunnnel2.0. Please plan accordingly as you need to make some change to you pac file to support Z-Tunnel2.0. Please refer to

About Z-Tunnel 1.0 & Z-Tunnel 2.0 | Zscaler

for the difference between ZTunnel1.0 and Ztunnel2.0.

Yes I am using ZCC method for traffic forwarding and using Z-Tunnel 1.0.

But I have seen if I disable “Block tunnelling to Non HTTP/HTTPS ports” it will inspect all ports and protocols. but don’t know what is the risk.

Choon_Ping_Koay

(Employee)

3 years ago

The option you mentioned is just disallow non 80/443 traffic to use HTTP CONNECT. If you want to cover all ports and protocols being forward to Zscaler cloud using ZCC, then Z-Tunnel2.0 is the option you have to go.

subham.ghorui

(Customer)

3 years ago

Okay Understood.

postalspin

(Customer)

3 years ago

If you build the tunnel from your client (laptop, desktop or sevrers) using ZCC, Tunnel 2.0 is able to capture all ports and protocols. Typical use case for this is Remote Workers (Road Warriors)

If you build the tunnel from a network device via GRE or IPSEC (Router, Firewall, SD-WAN etc) then you simply need to include the non 443 and 80 ports to go down the tunnel.

An alternative which I usually advise is to have you default route point down the tunnel to Zscaler, so by default everything goes via Zscaler and you exclude everything you dont want to hit Zscaler (Think MS Teams Voice, etc).

We were advised via our Technical Account Manager NOT to use Tunnel 2.0 mode on ZCC through a GRE/IPSEC tunnel as it is a suboptimal traffic path (something to do with Points of connectivity on the Zscaler cloud).

Hope that helps!

## ZCC Windows Client PCAP contains duplicates for every sent packet

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009eykLHCAY/zcc-windows-client-pcap-contains-duplicates-for-every-sent-packet
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-06-21T01:16:19.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

hukel

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

May 25, 2023 at 6:11 PM

ZCC Windows Client PCAP contains duplicates for every sent packet

We’re troubleshooting some client performance/stability issues and I have been looking at a lot of ZCC packet captures recently. I’ve noticed that every sent/outbound TCP packet is duplicated in the PCAP (within milliseconds of the original send, so I doubt these are retries).

Is this a known issue? Can it be corrected? It’s a real hassle to grab a PCAP and then have it full of meaningless red. It’s even worse if you show it to another vendor who uses it as an easy excuse to point the finger at Zscaler.

image

1474×359 41.8 KB

Client Connector

Discourse-expand

Far-image

5 answers

1.06K views

krogers

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hi Hugh,

The duplicate packets aren’t “real” in the sense that they are seen on the wire. It’s how some of the internals of Client Connector works.

You should be able to filter these packets out by using a display filter of

ip.checksum > 0x0006

. Then you can File > Export Specified Packets > Displayed and save as a new pcap. Open that pcap for a cleaner view.

HTH

hukel

(Customer)

3 years ago

Thank you, great hint. I found that had to use

ip.checksum != 0x0001

instead of

ip.checksum > 0x0006

(that wiped out the incoming packets), but I’ve got a much cleaner file now.

manuel

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hey Kary,

such info would REALLY be helpful if documented somewhere in the official KB.

BR

Manuel

krogers

(Employee)

3 years ago

Yes, I’ll see what we can do

krogers

(Employee)

3 years ago

https://zscaler-support.force.com/customers/s/article/How-to-remove-duplicate-packets-in-Zscaler-Client-Connector-LWF-packet-captures

How to achieve this without interrupting machine tunnel?

mharris30

(Employee)

3 years ago

Geeta - if I understand your requirement correctly, you can use the

Force Reauthentication

option in the ZIA Console under

Administration, Authentication Settings

. As for the machine tunnel, it exists separately from a user-authenticated session, so if you are forcing an active user to re-auth, it would not occur at the same time as a machine tunnel session anyway, so you wouldn’t be “interrupting machine tunnel” by using the forced re-auth procedure.

## ZCC Upgrade from 32bit to 64bit

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009eykLSCAY/zcc-upgrade-from-32bit-to-64bit
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-09-21T03:41:58.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

Gk

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

May 23, 2023 at 8:31 AM

ZCC Upgrade from 32bit to 64bit

We were upgrading our Zscaler client app from 3.7 to 4.1.0.85 version. We have mixure of 32bit and 64bit users using 3.7 version. When we upgrade via mobile portal, it affected ZPA access of few users. From the logs we notice Zscaler device posture is empty post upgrade. Our ZPA access policy blocks the connection which fails minimum posture.

Workaround:

a) ZCC → More → update policy

b) ZCC → More → restart service

c) ZCC → Relogin

d) Mobile portal → De-register/ register

We did few more testing to understand why few machine were affected and found this Upgrade path.

|a)|ZCC 3.7 64bit to 4.1 64bit upgrade via mobile portal => Working|

|b)|ZCC 3.7 32bit to 4.1 64bit upgrade via mobile portal => Not Working|

|c)|ZCC 3.7 32bit to 3.7 64bit to 4.1 64bit via mobile portal => Not Working|

|d)|ZCC 3.7 32bit to 4.0 64bit to 4.1 64bit via mobile portal => Working|

|e)|ZCC 3.7 32bit to 4.1 32bit to 4.1 64bit via mobile portal => Working|

|f)|ZCC 3.7 32bit to 4.1 64bit upgrade via SCCM Portal => Not Working|

|g)|ZCC 3.8 32bit to 4.1 64bit upgrade via mobile portal => Not Working|

|h)|ZCC 4.1 32bit to 4.1 64bit upgrade via mobile portal => Working|

Zscaler suggested to upgrade to 4.1.0.98 version which has fix. We are testing this upgrade path. Do anyone faced similar issue before or notice any issue with 4.1.0.98 version?

Client Connector

Thomas Scharl

(Customer)

3 years ago

A DHCP client sends out a broadcast to that IP when it wants to renew it’s IP address.

ZCC shouldn’t touch that traffic by any means, thus it needs to be added to the exclusion list.

Issue:

Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) disconnects frequently when the machine fails to get the IP address assigned to default interface and ZCC logs display “

No adapter found with default route. Trying IP Enabled approach

”.

Cause:

The issue occurs because the Client is unable to renew its address from the network (from the DHCP Server) and performing an ipconfig shows the network adapter not connected.

Solution:

DHCP uses broadcast address, and the connection should bypass Zscaler to get the address assigned.

Add “

255.255.255.255

” broadcast address under Destination Exclusions for IPv4 field in the App profile.

Reference for your admin:

https://zscaler-support.force.com/betacustomers/s/article/How-to-troubleshoot-Zscaler-client-connector-frequent-disconnection-issue-with-error-No-adapter-found-with-default-route-Trying-IP-Enabled-approach

Pat_Nicholson

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hello,

If I understand your question, the ‘Enable Build’ checkbox simply makes a specific version of ZCC available to your users. For instance, by navigating to the Update Setting section, you can see that there are 4 tabs. Always Latest, Specific Version, Group Based, and Disable. In this section is where you can leverage the versions that have been checked off in the ‘Enable Build’ column.

Pat

Thomas Scharl

(Customer)

3 years ago

additionally to what Pat already stated:

I would propose to go for ‘group based’ distribution.

This gives you the best control over when to distribute which specific ZCC version to which usergroup.

In best case distribute new versions in waves; starting with a handful of users, then 1-2weeks later a few dozen more, 1-2 weeks later a few hundred… with that IF anything strange pops up with a new version you will likely catch it before it hits your full user base.

A worst case scenario where you need to rollback to an older version (talking pre 3.9 days) because of a bug you didn’t catch early enough on 100s to 1000s of dewices aint fun; been there, done that

dcreedy

(Employee)

3 years ago

Pat and Thomas are correct here.

For background on this feature, it isn’t too uncommon that people have ‘latest version’ configured in update settings. The challenge there, while it might seem counterintuitive, is that when we release a new version those devices will update. This was added as a sort of ‘final gate’ where the approval for a new version, whether we enable it or not, is up to the administrator.

Internal Error Please Contact Administrator

Hello All, I have a user that has an HP Zbook 17 G8 and gets this error whenever he tries to log into Zscaler on it - Internal Error, Please Contact Administrator. Action: Ensure that the version of Zscaler Client Connector is current. Check that traffic is not being modified between the device and the server. - The options are Learn more and OK. I have uninstalled and reinstalled the latest version zscaler twice, making sure that I restart the computer before reinstalling zscaler again. I have run all HP driver updates and Windows updates as well. I had the user sign into zscaler on another computer and he had no issues, so it must be that computer itself. I could just reimage the users Zbook computer but the user has very expensive software on it that would require re-licensing that software again and that is very painful process. G-Man8

Hi David,

Have you checked the OS WMI health of the device in question ?

Joe.ps1

(Customer)

3 years ago

I noticed in recent ZCC versions, some of the specific error numbers have been removed which makes it difficult to troubleshoot the root cause. I had the same error on a machine recently and it was because WMI was broken on the machine as G-Man suggests.

Test WMI by running this command in an Admin cmdprompt (or PowerShell)

wmic ComputerSystem get Name

If the command does not return your Computer’s name, WMI is broken. Save these commands as a text file and name it FixWMI.bat then run as an admin to rebuild the WMI repositories:

@echo off

sc config winmgmt start= disabled

net stop winmgmt /y

%systemdrive%

cd %windir%\system32\wbem

for /f %%s in ('dir /b *.dll') do regsvr32 /s %%s

wmiprvse /regserver

winmgmt /regserver

sc config winmgmt start= auto

net start winmgmt

for /f %%s in ('dir /s /b *.mof *.mfl') do mofcomp %%s

Reference:

WMI: Rebuilding the WMI Repository - Microsoft Community Hub

Pardeep09

(Partner)

3 years ago

Here you have another option to repair ad rebuild the WMI, to run below shared command in CMD with admin privilege.

cd C:\Windows\System32\wbem & dir /b *.mof *.mfl | findstr /v /i uninstall > moflist.txt & for /F %s in (moflist.txt) do mofcomp %s

Hey dvestlie,

I've encountered similar issues before with Zscaler on HP devices. It's frustrating, I know. From your description, it sounds like you've covered the basics

by reinstalling

Zscaler and ensuring all updates are in place. Since the user didn't face issues on another computer, it's likely a local problem.

One thing to check is the firewall settings on the HP Zbook 17 G8. Sometimes, they can interfere with Zscaler's connections. Ensure that the firewall isn't blocking any traffic related to Zscaler.

Additionally, try running Zscaler in compatibility mode or as an administrator. Sometimes, this helps resolve internal errors.

If these steps don't work, reach out to Zscaler support. They might have additional troubleshooting steps or insights specific to their software.

Hang in there! These issues can be a pain, but with a bit of patience and persistence, we'll get it sorted without resorting to a full reimage.

remov

2 years ago

This topic might be old, many users might still face this issue with disconnect and reconnect every moment. And this might be helpful to some.

As a Desktop Engineer, recently I was facing this issue, Zscaler was flapping, disconnected/reconnected, many other users were facing the same issue from one org.

It does not matter if you are a Mac user, a linux or windows. It is not a device issue.

It is not a Zscaler issue or maybe it is a Zscaler issue.

This is purely a network one.

So here is my finding.

The problem itself is not with Zscaler.  Zscaler is doing what should be done correctly to protect the networks or applications. The problem is with the IP range. (similar ip at two different location/network)

At the

Corporate Org  XYZ

we had Users or maybe all users were facing this. It all comes down to IP address and maybe geo location.

Example:

Real case…

You are connecting from different geolocation at different time.

Those location they have IP range as below...

1.     Organization XYZ  (ip: 10.x.x.x/xx)

2.     You are working home Office (HO) (ip: 10.x.x.x/xx)

3.     You are in a public space, at your favorite caffee, restaurant or park (ip: 10.x.x.x/xx)

Three different geolocations take account of that and three simlar ip range..

a.     Location 1. XYZ you have a network (intranet) with ip private ip 10.X.X.X/xx

b.     You may have VPN too.

You logged on in the office and you have no issue. Zscaler is not flapping.

An hour later you move to

HO.

You connect your device to your home network – wifi or lan and it start to disconnect and reconnect or  you move from the Office to public place over the free wifi.

At this point Zscaler start to disconnect and reconnect, ‘not trusted network ‘ or something like that you will see.

Why is this happening according to my findings?

1 At the office you the private ip 10.x.x.x./xx

2. at home also when your ISP provided you with a router, 90%  the default IP is 10.x.x.x/x (Private IP) and you have not changed it.

At home you have control over the ip range ,  to change it.

At the office you don’t have control, at the park you do not have control over the ip setting.

To my assumption from what I have observed the private IP range is in conflict, Zscaler is seeing the same number 10.x.x.x/xx and it might be literally saying’ hey, an hour ago you were at geolocation ABC, now  an hour later you are at a different geolocationn BYC  with the same IP range’.

So, the issue starts.

To fix this you have two options.

Option 1#. You have control over you home router/gateway.

You just have to log on  to your gateway and change the IP range to something else, do not use the 10.x.x.x/xx or 192.168.x.x.x.  as the one in office, Just any other IP rang, then reboot the router.

This should rectify the issue, no more disconnecting or reconnecting from Zscaler. Now Zscaler is trusting the new IP which is not the same as the one in the office.

Option 2#. If you have VPN and are away from office.

First connect to the VPN. This will bring your connection back to the office, then out through Zscaler to your world of apps and security.

This is my approach.  I really resolved this issue with Zscaler disconnecting and reconnecting.

It is as if Zscaler is treating those identical private ip (the numbers) from different location as ip spoofing – or false ip spoofing.

Nevertheless, you might get the reverse with the flapping in office

Case: you have spent all your working hours or several months at home Zscaler trust your home ip 10.x.x.x/xx, then all of a sudden you go to the office and connect through the office network and it start to flaps as it sees a new geolocation with the identical private IP.

Before you do anything take note of the location you are getting the disconnection, at home, in the office, public place.

Then, from the CMD, do an ‘ipconfig /all’ , check your preferred ipv4.. This will give you or your tech a lot of info.

To cut it short, this is my observation and implementation to all my users who came to me.

So said.

Ipconfig /all for the record.

Then change your home ip to another range.

For data/hotspot connection I have not gone into that yet.

But there is another question here which arise..?! another discussion..??!!.

danl

(Customer)

5 months ago

On a number of laptop PC's I have solved this problem by going to the

network adapter device driver properties

and turning

OFF

any kind of idle/power related energy saving features. Thus giving Zscaler a more continuous network connection for it's health/heartbeat monitoring. These PCs went from constantly logging connect/disconnect entries and constantly having disconnect notification popups to having practically none.

## ZCC Versions Consfusion

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009eykQECAY/zcc-versions-consfusion
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-06-05T04:51:35.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

jlw52761

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

March 30, 2023 at 7:50 PM

ZCC Versions Consfusion

Maybe this has been asked before, but I can’t find it.

Why does Zscaler maintain 3 Major/Minor versions of ZCC? I understand General Availability (GA) vs Limited Availability (RC), but why 3.9, 4.0, and 4.1?

This really is a bit confusing when trying to determine what version I should be pushing to my users. Even more so when I open a case with Zscaler and their answer is to upgrade to the 4.1 version of ZCC, which is all in Limited Availability and really shouldn’t be run in production, IMHO.

Client Connector

Discourse-expand

Far-image

1.48K views

Ben_Snowden

likes this.

Syazwan

(Partner)

3 years ago

Hi

@jlw52761

IMHO, Zscaler just maintain the record of ZCC released, perhaps because of readiness of many customer to perform upgrade.

Some organization has strict upgrade process, in order to release the upgrade to all users, intensive test is pilot and run with smaller batch of users first, before specific ZCC version release to all users.

But why the question? the practice always best n-1 version, when you notice there is new version, then it is time to pilot n-1 version in your/customer ground.

my2cent.

jlw52761

(Customer)

3 years ago

So I agree with N-1, but when there’s a 3.9, 4.0, and 4.1 line, each with sub-releases, which line do you maintain N-1 on? There’s active releases in both the 3.9 and 4.0 lines, so what’s the difference between the two and when would one run 3.9 vice 4.0?

Syazwan

(Partner)

3 years ago

Ah perhaps I didn’t understand the earlier question, seems like your asking why Zscaler still providing minor release under major line.

From what I noticed, those patch release comes with only ‘Fixes’, below is how I read the release.

3.9.0.189

3 = Major

3.9 = Minor

3.9.x.x = Patches

And, perhaps Zscaler provided the patches for customer that not ready for major/minor upgrade yet. With patches version, the impact will be much less than major/minor release.

Just another my2cent.

Thomas Scharl

(Customer)

3 years ago

agree on this being confusing.

Also from the release notes it is not always really clear which are the new features which will not be backported to the other major versions.

Neither i’ve ever seen any statement like ‘this is the last version ever for eg v3.7/v3.8 stream’. Can only assume that there will be no newer v3.8 as the last one is now 9 months old…

Would be much easier with a system like

x..n.n → new feature development

x..n.n → no new feaures, only fixes

(one hint when to better use 4.0 over 3.9 … if you use ZPA and do a posture check for Defender → you DO want 4.0, trust me

jlw52761

(Customer)

3 years ago

So being a developer, I do understand Semantic Versioning, which is typically {Major}.{Minor}.{Patch}. Zscaler seems to be using a modified version of this where it’s {Major}.{Minor}.0.{Patch}, which seems odd but not completely crazy.

My question centers more around why are they keeping two Major versions (3 & 4) alive? This can be due to compatibility reasons, where there’s some breaking change between the Major versions, but there’s 0 indication of this in the documentation anywhere.

The 3.9 line seems to be active as it’s still getting patches, and is the 4.0 line. The 4.1 lines seems to introduce some new features, like Path MTU, but is still a “Limited Availability” release, which screams Beta or Release Candidate, without the typical BETA or RC suffix.

The base for this question is, most of my users are running the 3.9.0.189 version, but there’s some oddities in our environment, so we have been limited testing the 4.0.0.89 version, because honestly I don’t know if that’s the next jump or if a new 3.9.0.x version is released. Well, there was a 3.9.0.191 version released, so it appears that the 3.9.0.x version is still being updated, just not getting the new features of the 4.0.0.x version, which leads me to believe that 3.9.0.x is on the way out, but does that mean the entire 3.x version is on the way out, or is there a 3.10 version planned that would compel me to stay with the 3.x version? I do see a 3.9.0.160 AND 3.8.0.x sitting in both GA and Limited Availability, so does that mean 3.8.0.x is still viable and supported? Should I be running that instead of any others?

This gets even more confusing because on 4.0.0.89, there’s a bug where when booting up, a user can receive an “Internal Error” and have to manually interact with ZCC to get it working. Support says I need to upgrade to 4.1.0.89 because there’s a fix for that there, but the 4.1.0.x line isn’t GA, so why would support say for me to upgrade to that unless there’s some undocumented thing coming that says 3.x and 4.0.0.x are going away? Is the fix not being backported to 4.0.0.x? Is 3.x going to die on the vine and we should plan to upgrade out users to the 4.0.0.x line IF this bug gets backported?

I get having the current version go into a maintenance mode, but usually there’s some documentation that says, in this case, 3.x is a LTS release that is in Extended Maintenance Release, also that 4.0.0.x is the CURRENT release and there are plans to move to the 4.1.0.x line and replace the 4.0.0.x, for example. None of that exists for Zscaler.

And when talking N-1, I don’t do that for only Major or Minor releases, but for patches. So, staying by that, I think the right answer is to stay at 3.9.0.x, but, if there’s features of 4.1 that we requires, such as Path MTU Discovery, then we can update to that once it becomes GA because it’s not a .0 release in regards to the Minor version number and it’s received a number of Patches. Again, no documentation to support any of this, so it’s a guessing game.

I would recommend that if you use Windows and ZPA, have a script ready to go to disable IPv6 on your adapters. - Type: Q&A

ZIA - Authentication

User16788984827242511944

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

March 22, 2023 at 11:52 PM

ZIA Client Connector Auth via Azure SSO Question

Hello all,

Before I get started down this road, I’d like to verify if this is possible.

Recently I set up our ZScaler Admins to SSO via Azure and it works great (we have on-prem AD and Azure AD sync). Now I’d like to do that with Client Connector users. What I’m after is for the Client Connector authentication to be completely seamless and transparent to the end user. We have machines that multiple users will log into during the day and I’d like their Client Connector sessions to automatically authenticate based upon their Windows authentication. I don’t want my end users interacting with the agent at all.

Is that something that works out there?

Thanks in advance!

ZIA - Authentication

2 answers

862 views

mryan

(Employee)

3 years ago

Yes. Provided Azure SSO works in the browser, it’ll work for ZCC.

For example - Azure using password hash sync, and hybrid joined device, will receive a PRT when the user logs on. This will be passed during Zscaler SSO to

login.microsoftonline.com

, and the user transparently authenticated.

Example video is here

Azure SAML Managed vs unmanaged - YouTube

- but this is also doing MFA for unmanaged devices.

## okta oie zscaler auto-enrollment

- Type: Q&A

Client Connector

vikas.tiwari

(Customer) asked a question.

June 26, 2023 at 5:51 PM

okta oie zscaler auto-enrollment

Hello Zscaler users,

We have Okta integration in place with Zscaler. User is able to login to Zscaler Client Connector using there Okta credentials and the login works fine. But in this process the enrollment is really slow and we want to speed up the enrollment with current step up.

With Okta OIE and Okta Verify/Fastpass have someone done some setup using which user don't have to interact with Zscaler Client Connector login or Okta login page and as soon as Zscaler Client Connector is installed on the machine it logs in automatically. We can't use Machine Tunnel in our setup.

Thank you in advance.

Client Connector

5 answers

700 views

Ben_Garrison

(Employee)

3 years ago

@Niladri_Datta

(Employee)

​  do you have any suggestions for performance improvements?

Niladri_Datta

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hi Vikas - There are a couple of options to reduce user interaction in your situation.

When ZCC runs for the first time, it will initially prompt the user to enter their username before redirecting to your IdP. You can remove this prompt with the use of --userDomain and --cloudName during installation. Check out this help

article

After the above is complete, ZCC redirects the user to your IdP and prompts them to login. In order to leverage Seamless SSO and remove the need for the user to login to Okta, you can leverage Okta DSSO in an Agent or Agentless deployment. Please review Okta documentation regarding this feature.

Hope this helps

vikas.tiwari

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hi Niladri,

I am using --userDomain and --cloudName options.

when I am access okta dashboard Okta Verify/fastpass recognizes it and allows the silent login without interacting with login page. But when zscaler as Service Provider sends it to Okta, user has to click on

Sign in with Okta FastPass.

I am wondering if there is a way user don't have to click on that button to invoke okta verify when sent to okta login page from ZCC.

Niladri_Datta

(Employee)

3 years ago

Zscaler Client Connector uses the embedded system browser to redirect the user to Okta and waits for authentication to complete and receive the SAML assertions from Okta.

During login, Okta policies  dictate the user experience.  You will need to configure Okta for the desired behavior.

vikas.tiwari

(Customer)

3 years ago

If you have some documentation which I can use to configure Okta is such a way that SP initiated flow allows direct login without interaction will be helpful.

## Zscaler Client Connector (macOS) - Pulse Secure - VPN Trusted Network Adapter Criteria

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009pTkGeCAK/zscaler-client-connector-macos-pulse-secure-vpn-trusted-network-adapter-criteria
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-08-02T13:09:30.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

Collin

(Partner) asked a question.

August 1, 2023 at 7:15 PM

Zscaler Client Connector (macOS) - Pulse Secure - VPN Trusted Network Adapter Criteria

Customer is using full tunnel on Pulse Secure.

Want to disable ZIA when user connects to Pulse Secure VPN. Has anyone done this?

adding "Pulse" and "Pulse Secure" to the VPN Trusted Network Adapter Criteria is not working.

Works fine off VPN with ZT2.0 DTLS

ZIA - Forwarding

2 answers

470 views

Thomas Scharl

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hi,

a combination of using 'HOSTNAME OR IP ADDRESS BYPASS FOR VPN GATEWAY' in app profiles, 'TRUSTED NETWORK CRITERIA' in forward profiles and/or 'trusted network' in mobile portal being set to your needs.

So more or less like 'exclude your VPN concentrator IPs in app profile' and 'define what your trusted networks are' via trusted network settings should do the trick.

We eg use 'dns search domains' as decission point if a user is connected onprem or offprem.

Hope that helps.

tS

Collin

(Partner)

3 years ago

We do use trusted networks for when on prem. When Off prem ZIA should be enabled as well.  But when connected to VPN it should be disabled. The Trusted Network Adapter Criteria is not working for Junos on MacOS.

## Long Standing Captive Portal Issue

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009rbEiQCAU/long-standing-captive-portal-issue
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-08-24T16:14:32.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

Ryan_N

(Customer) asked a question.

August 9, 2023 at 2:43 AM

Long Standing Captive Portal Issue

Would like to start another thread for conversation on Captive Portal issues that are experienced for people on Windows Clients

I have ample findings on this issue and there are several different threads hosted elsewhere that all seem to point the fingers at ZIA regardless of what configurations people are running and ZCC versions. This is supported in the fact that I had P1 case open with Zscaler for weeks but had to close it due Microsoft April KIR.

Without diving too deep into my specific config I would like to state that issue is relevant on every Zscaler Client Connector App version from 3.6.0.26 to 4.2.0.190.

I would also like to ask what other solutions people have come to because at this point my direction has deemed CrowdStrike more beneficial to our end points than Zscaler traffic forwarding and users that travel contact me directly instead of our Care Center to resolve this. I have consulted with other Zscaler administrators possible resolutions that weren't effective for my environment.

Something I have noticed in my recent testing is that it seems CrowdStrike(Falcon) firewall appears to have an impact on this as I can turn it to monitor mode and the issue is no longer relevant. Falcon takes the place of Windows Defender on our workstations which has policy for the Captive Portal that is forced by Zscaler. With Captive Portal off, this issue does not go away. I have a ticket open with CrowdStrike as well because this configuration doesn't come with more than "allow all" or "block all". I would be very interested if other customers who have experienced this issue also have CrowdStrike active or something alternative to Defender.

Thanks in advance and lets try to keep this conversation headed in towards progress while addressing an issue that has previously gone unsolved on this portal. My primary goal is to get traffic forwarding enabled on these users ASAP.

Ryan

ZIA - Forwarding

2.49K views

Hey Ryan,

Zscaler Client Connector 4.2.0.198 Enhancements and Fixes

Fixes a user access control issue by enforcing more validations when handling log files.

Fixes a UI issue where the PIN dialog for smart card authentication hid behind the Zscaler tray in some scenarios.

Fixes a latency issue with web traffic by enhancing DNS handling capability in Zscaler Client Connector.

Fixes an issue with Microsoft Defender Antivirus device posture in a localized environment.

Fixes an issue where the captive portal page was displayed even when the

captive portal detection was disabled

in the Zscaler Client Connector Portal.

https://help.zscaler.com/client-connector/client-connector-app-release-summary-2023?applicable_category=Windows

We had no issues with Captive Portals/Detection and MDATP so far but thinking about extending/replacing the latter by CS.

Will update this thread if this happens to be the golden ticket!

GordonWright

(Customer)

3 years ago

ZCC v4.3 available in Limited Availability which has some Captive Portal improvements.

david.ma1

(Customer)

3 years ago

4.3 will allow the ability for the user to launch captive portal in a browser.

The recommendation from Zscaler support is now to remove all CP landing page URL's out of the PAC and Bypasses.

The question really is whether Captive Portal Detection is triggering. If it doesn't even trigger then Zscaler needs to identify why.

Even with all this setup correctly if you are using Crowdstrike there is also a concern. Our company enforces a blacklist default posture for outbound traffic on CS. So you can imagine trying to figure out what ports or destination any CP uses is a pain to manage on CS.

And then after all this... there are still some issues with Captive Portals regardless.

Ryan_N

(Customer)

3 years ago

So, in our scenario there are virtually no issues with captive portal when either CrowdStrike Firewall or Zscaler Client Connector are out of the picture. Unfortunately, of the two tools Zscaler was the one that was deemed as the pressure release until I resolve this issue. As we get further away from Covid times we have more and more operations that require more and more people to travel. Causing a large uptick in calls to our care center and out CC is not equipped to tackle these issues to no fault of their own.

I have followed the allow list documentation Zscaler provides but have been able to identify CrowdStrike is blocking all inbound communications while on the captive portal. We have inbound set to block all - but I was understanding that the exclusions would allow certain functionalities from not triggering at all.

I have a call with a CS rep that states familiarity in the realm and is confident we can resolve this in our next call. I also have a test object I have created where I add rfc1918 IPs to the ZSATunnel.exe rule as all the denies I see to this are coming from RFC1918. But, I am not confident that all the hotels are the same and not using public IPs for rooms.

Ryan_N

(Customer)

3 years ago

So I am pretty sure I have resolved this from a CrowdStrike perspective. Of 120 testers, I have a single report of continued issues with captive portal.. And the end user didn't respond to my follow-up so it may have been user error. I have also included users that connect standard to ensure no negative impact before I throw at prod.

I really hope that others can come to resolution here as well as this issue has been plaguing all of our field agents for longer than I have been with the company..

We just had to make an adjustment to our CrowdStrike firewall allow list to a different variant of glob-syntax seen below. We did this for all the executables and has worked better since.

**\Program Files*\

Zscaler\ZSATunnel\ZSATunnel.exe

I hope all can resolve as I have!

## ZCC client strict enforcement not working?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009sVdQfCAK/zcc-client-strict-enforcement-not-working
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-08-23T01:26:50.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

Tmc9

(Customer) asked a question.

August 16, 2023 at 3:18 PM

ZCC client strict enforcement not working?

I'm trying to deploy the ZCC client in strict enforcement mode. I have defined the msi parameter --strictEnforcement per documentation (

https://help.zscaler.com/client-connector/customizing-zscaler-client-connector-install-options-msi

), and I have a policy token and all prerequisites defined per documentation using tunnel with local proxy. The ZCC client shows it is in strict enforcement mode.

One problem - it isn't blocking the internet. I'm wanting the strict enforcement behavior of blocking internet access until the ZCC client is logged into, however, with the ZCC client in strict enforcement mode, the internet is still fully accessible.

I have opened a ticket with support to assist in troubleshooting this, however, I wanted to check with the community and see if anyone had any ideas. Has anyone run into this?

ZIA - Forwarding

8 answers

3.38K views

G-Man8

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hi,

We use strict enforcement via the MSI but using 'Tunnel' which works 100%.

Could it be something in your 'Local Proxy' config/PAC that allows the bypass ?

Possible to test by doing a command line based installation using another PolicyToken for an App Profile you can change to 'Tunnel' ?

Tmc9

(Customer)

3 years ago

Unfortunately, we have to use tunnel with local proxy enabled due to technical requirements. Pure tunnel is not an option for our environment.

mrockey

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hey! Is this behavior consistent across multiple devices? Could you try a different (maybe older) version of the client connector?

david.ma1

(Customer)

3 years ago

Strict enforcement also requires a policy token of a dedicated app profile you created for Strict Enforcement. The app profile should include 0.0.0.0/0 as an inclusion to always tunnel.

Tmc9

(Customer)

3 years ago

Interesting, so you must always tunnel internet bound traffic? Is this stated in the documentation anywhere?

mrockey

(Employee)

3 years ago

That should be default in the app profile. It does get me thinking, is IPv6 enabled on your computer? Or do you have IPv6 dropped in the forwarding profile?

joemozdy

(Customer)

3 years ago

If you have anything set up in the "HOSTNAME OR IP ADDRESS BYPASS FOR VPN GATEWAY" field in the app profile page, or applications like Teams or Zoom that you are bypassing from the Client Connector in the app profile you are using when installing, users will be able to navigate to any of those destinations/use those applications. Try calling a more restrictive policy during install with the POLICYTOKEN argument, that has the user groups and users set to None in the app profile. Then, when users authenticate through the Client Connector, they will get assigned your normal or standard app profile.

Tmc9

(Customer)

3 years ago

Yeah, and we have a few - but we certainly don't have the general internet whitelisted, and users are able to get to that while the zcc client reports it is in strict enforcement mode.

## Detect STRICRENFORCEMENT

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009ttNOdCAM/detect-stricrenforcement
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-06-11T18:17:10.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

RAC

(Customer) asked a question.

August 18, 2023 at 3:02 PM

Detect STRICRENFORCEMENT

Is it possible to detect if ZCC is installed with the STRICTENFORCEMENT option? We want to be able to check that all installs are correctly configured for STRICTENFORCEMENT and if not initiate a reinstallation of ZCC with the correct options.

Client Connector

7 answers

3.78K views

Top Rated Answers

GordonWright

(Customer)

3 years ago

There is a registry key you can look at to see if strict enforcement is enbaled:

- Search for the registry key "Computer\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Zscaler Inc.\Zscaler"

- Edit the key called "Enforce" and set this to

99

(any other number sets Strict Enforcement to Enabled)

Selected as Best

Zscaler ZCC prompt the username page, which is for identify the where this company is provisioned in Zscaler like,

zscaler.net

zscalertwo.net

zscalerthree.net

and so on.  The next action is with "userdomain" which helps to understand the company details and what type of authentication is enabled on the zscaler console. So while pushing the package to client with cloud name and userdomain will helps to identify the company details, on which cloud it is provisioned, which is the authentication mechanism. So ZCC will landup with IDP authentication. If your IDP provisioned in a way that to handle SSO, transparent authentication will happen.

(Partner) asked a question.

August 30, 2023 at 3:11 PM

PAC file proxy statement for Z-Tunnel 2.0

Hello,

I have a technical doubt regarding Pac file and Z-Tunnel 2.0. We have Z-Tunnel 2.0 configured on App profile/FW Profile.

On the Pac file we've configured this statements for default traffic forwarding:

PROXY ${COUNTRY_GATEWAY_FX}:80

What I understand is the following:

Web traffic generated by browsers (that have knowledge of Pac file) will flow to port 80 on the end user device

This traffic will get captured by Client Connector

Cli Conn will forward this traffic using DTLS to ZEN

Is this correct? I'm a bit confused regarding the port used at the end of the proxy statement :80 as we are using Z-Tunnel 2.0 I think we should use port 443 may be? But if this is only local traffic at the end it will be captured by Client Connector.

Thanks for your time :)

Regards,

ZIA - Forwarding

2 answers

596 views

Tachyon2

likes this.

Dustin

(Customer)

3 years ago

That is the port that client will use to connect to the Zscaler public service edge.

You can change the port if you like, more info:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/writing-pac-file#return-statements

Tachyon2

(Customer)

2 years ago

@Luis Arizaga​ In case this is still a relevant question for you, when you're using ZCC, the browser on the host will not be aware of the PAC file. Rather, it just assumes that things are normal, using normal ports (typically 80 or 443, depending on HTTP type of the parsed URL), except for the local proxy that's configured typically (TWLP).

ZCC will grab this traffic, and will then forward it using the port defined in the RETURN statement in the PAC file. The connection that ZCC uses will be a DTLS (UDP, or TLS-in-TCP) tunnel (with no encryption) to that defined port. The browser won't be aware of the port used by the ZCC-to-ZEN tunnel.

Update your browser / Unsupported Browser Error in ZScaler Client Connector During First Login

We have been experiencing an issue with the embedded browser within ZScaler Client Connector.

Users that try to authenticate to ZScaler Client Connector on a machine for the first time receive this error message:

We are using Azure AD as our IdP.

Has anyone else experienced this issue? If so, were you able to find a fix?

Support recommended we try enabling WebView 2.0 in the Platform Settings in the ZCC admin GUI; however, it does not seem to support the Azure AD Conditional Access Policy that checks to see if the computer you are logging in from is domain-joined so authentication fails.

ZCC App Version: 4.2.0.190

ZIA - Authentication

3 answers

4.23K views

GordonWright

(Customer)

3 years ago

That message is coming from your IdP I think.

What Conditional Access is it failing?

mrockey

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hi!

What type of MFA is it asking for? The embedded browser only supports some MFA types, and not things like biometric.

Something you might try is enabling Browser Based Authentication. What this does is pop the SSO authentication out to the default system browser rather than run it in the embedded browser. This will give you full MFA support. This is a global setting though, so ensure the proper change management is happening before it is enabled as it will effect everyone who tries to login to ZCC.

https://help.zscaler.com/client-connector/about-authentication-settings

Cows_with_JetPacks

(Customer)

3 years ago

Thank you

@mrockey

(Employee)

​ and

@GordonWright

(Customer)

​ for the replies and suggestions.

Yes, the error message was from the IdP. ZCC was using IE 11 as its User Agent by default, and I believe we weren't allowing logins from IE 11.

What ultimately fixed the issue for us was adding Edg/120.0.2210.89 as the User Agent which makes it appear to be the latest version of Edge browser.

See here for where to locate the User Agent setting:

Customizing Zscaler Client Connector User Agent | Zscaler

So the that address is not Zscaler ---- its RFC 6598 --- it is used by Tier 1 carrier which Zscaler to move data or transaction between data centers and nodes ----

If you seeing the 100.64.0.0/16 addresses

Do you have Zscaler Private Access and our you Source IP Anchoring with Zscaler between ZIA and ZPA ?

Kaija

(Customer)

3 years ago

Also if the Problem is MACs --- did you set up MAC postures and and client checks to turn off Zscaler Private Access on premise keep in mind if the device is not supervised in the MDM and all installs come from the MDM this may not actually turn off

So something to keep in lock step between the teams so one tenant does not break the other

GordonWright

(Customer)

3 years ago

Either way we should NEVER see 100.64.0.0/16 as the source IP address.

Kaija

(Customer)

3 years ago

Correct --- the other rub here is what Tunnel set up is running on the clients --- DTLS 2.0 - will by default take all ports all protocols up up to Zscaler unless you specifically deny them access to say like DNS  --- say your clients leverage Umbrella Secure DNS from Cisoc - via the AnyConnect security module or the Umbrella client --

You would this documentation from Cisco ---

https://support.umbrella.com/hc/en-us/articles/230563527-Using-Umbrella-with-an-HTTP-proxy

to set up your DNS exclusions in the APP and Forwarding profiles for the Umbrella destinations

so that they get treated basically the same treatment  as like a Citrix or VPN portal

that addresses one piece there is in newer agents going to be settings specific to the 100.64 in the ZCC configuration to watch for them

Kaija

(Customer)

3 years ago

Another thing past ZIA/ZPA to SIPA --- there is also Browser Isolation  or Browser Access --- that runs off ZPA that can use the 100.64.0.0/16 internally

There are ways to see this in ZIA logging -- look for traffic from these clients using Traffic Forwarding / Forwarding Methord - Gateway Name / etc

October 17, 2023 at 12:40 AM

iOS - Strict Enforment

Hi All,

We are using workspace one UEM (AirWatch from VMWare) and are trying to get strict enforcement to work on Apple iPhones. We have used custom settings based in https://help.zscaler.com/z-app/deploying-zscaler-app-workspace-one-uem-ios and test users are able to browse the internet still.

Has anyone got it to work with it or Global HTTP Proxy was used to do strict enforcement with a PAC file created in the console? Thank you for any guidance :)

Client Connector

2 answers

542 views

Niladri_Datta

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hi -

Here is a sample Profile XML (attached) you can import right into WorkspaceONE UEM to check out StrictEnforcement on iOS. Please make sure to make the below changes before importing to WorkspaceONE.

Update the "cloudname" value

Update the "excludeList" value with hostname for your MDM and IdP value

Create an App Profile PAC with the sample bypasses as excludeList above and assign it to the App Profile referenced by the policyToken below

Update the "userDomain" value

Update the "policyToken" value

Unknown file type

zscaler-strict-enforcement

KB

(Customer) asked a question.

October 19, 2023 at 12:50 PM

How to connect to another Zscaler VPN when my company uses Zscaler without having to uninstall and reinstall

Our company uses Zscaler as our VPN. I am required to support customers who also use Zscaler.

How can I keep my company VPN on and login to another Zscaler account.

Currently I have to uninstall and reinstall Zscaler Client Connector to be able to login to the other VPN.

When I am needing to log back into my company Zscaler client will not allow me to login to the other company after I log back out of my company. I have to uninstall and reinstall.

Logging in always launches my companies profile for logging in and does not give me an option to login to the clients vpn.

Is there a way to run multiple instances of Zscaler or at least have 2 VPN profiles i can login and log out without having to uninstall and reinstall?

Client Connector

## Automated Device Cleanup

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000A6UxuRCQS/automated-device-cleanup
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-10-29T22:45:06.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

Bob_Pants

(Customer) asked a question.

October 27, 2023 at 12:15 AM

Automated Device Cleanup

I am about to enable Automated Device Cleanup in the CC portal.

Under the 'Automatically force removal of inactive devices' section, the tip says "If a device connects to the system after removal, it is logged out". - What does this mean? the documentation says nothing further on this.

If a device gets removed after inactivity, it is never allowed back on again?  So what happens if this occurs, how do we resolve this situation?

Client Connector

1 answer

508 views

Top Rated Answers

Niladri_Datta

(Employee)

3 years ago

A removed device can re-enroll by logging back into Client Connector. If you "Quarantine" the device however, then the device can't log back in until you remove it from quarantine

Selected as Best

2 likes

Niladri_Datta

3 years ago

A removed device can re-enroll by logging back into Client Connector. If you "Quarantine" the device however, then the device can't log back in until you remove it from quarantine

## ZCC deletion with admin access

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AA1RYoCQN/zcc-deletion-with-admin-access
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-12-07T23:26:57.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

ShriSivakumaran

(Customer) asked a question.

November 21, 2023 at 4:47 PM

ZCC deletion with admin access

We can move Zscaler folders which is in applications folder in macOS with admin rights even if we enabled password protection. Is there anyway to protect Zscaler folder not to delete in macOS?

Client Connector

5 answers

402 views

GordonWright

(Customer)

3 years ago

Does the Anti-Tampering option work on macOS?

GordonWright

(Customer)

3 years ago

Anti-Tampering for Zscaler Client Connector | Zscaler

ShriSivakumaran

(Customer)

3 years ago

Tamper is enabled, even though we able to move the Zscaler folder to Trash/Bin with local admin credentials in macOS

CKAIJA

(Employee)

3 years ago

I would think that would be working as designed - your user is the LOCAL ADMIN of the MAC not a user, and if the user is logged in as the actual Administrator of the MAC - they have all rights to do as they will with the File tree and the applications on the MAC.

Now if I you were to install it say under MDM like AirWatch, MobileIron, JAMF, and the User was just a USER and not given Admin rights then I would think that your issue would not be present

So I think this issue comes down to  how are your MACs deployed and is all users are given Administrator level  rights, you would need to look into restricting those rights to folders on the MAC OS that you do not want them to manipulate or change.

1 like

dcreedy

(Employee)

3 years ago

As users with root are intended to have full control over the system, they will be able to move files around yes. Anti Tampering on Windows for example, is more targeted towards tampering coming from the user space (which is traditionally a simpler task on Windows).

You might have noticed the new option in the App Profiles below to compliment the 'Authenticate Early' feature along with your ZPA timeout Policies.

Notify Users before ZPA Authentication Expires: Enable this option to alert users that applications they recently accessed through Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) are going to expire. December 4, 2023 at 5:07 PM

ZCC HTTP Authentication Redirects

We have deployed ZCC but we still see HTTP 307 redirects for authentication when using a browser.

We assumed that there won't be any 307 anymore because authentication takes place in ZCC.

Did we miss something?

Client Connector

1 answer

909 views

dcreedy

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hi,

I don't think there should be a 307 redirect. Can you expand on how/where you are seeing this? Client Connector should remove the need for any auth prompts in the browser yes, the only exception to this would be if Client Connector was deployed with "enforce proxy", instead of tunneling, in which case we are just apply a pac file to the browser pointing to ZIA, in this mode you would still be doing cookie auth.

## Traffic Bypass From Zscaler

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ACCSNMCQ5/traffic-bypass-from-zscaler
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-01-11T12:54:29.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

Dhananjay_Bhakte

(Partner) asked a question.

December 10, 2023 at 11:24 AM

Traffic Bypass From Zscaler

Hi,

Good Day !

Can someone kindly explain,

As we know we can define in Zscaler profile that what type of traffic to keep away from client connector.

So to define this in Zscaler, traffic should first reach to ZCC. Now my query is, when traffic is already reaching to ZCC then what is the meaning to define "keep traffic away from ZCC"

Is this my understanding is correct?

Thanks

Dhananjay

Client Connector

3 answers

946 views

Top Rated Answers

dcreedy

(Employee)

3 years ago

Generally 'Keep away from the client', would mean we are configuring the machine to not send traffic to Client Connector at all, which is different to having it reach Client Connector and then be bypassed.

A good example of this is the VPN Gateway Bypass vs. the Ztunnel 2 Excludes.

VPN Gateway Bypass instructs the operating system (either via route table entry or packet filter entry) to not send the traffic to the client

Ztunnel 2 excludes, the traffic is still received by the client but then bypassed/sent direct.

Selected as Best

1 like

All Answers

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

3 years ago

Hi Dhananjay,

Traffic reach at ZCC doesn't mean is breakout from user machines, still we have options to bypass from ZCC and breakout locally.

Certain traffic may not require going via Zscaler service edge,

For example,

1) internal traffic not necessary to go to Zscaler

2) Destination URL may require source validation,

3) geo graphical needs to breakout traffic locally.

Regards

MsTeam & Outlook doesn't work in ZCC 4.2 when Window Defender Isolate the machine

Windows Defender Service level isolation is used to quarantine the unpatched machine. This option will allow end user to still use MsTeams and Outlook even after isolation. Ben_Garrison

(Employee)

2 years ago

Are you leveraging any application bypass policies?

Gk

(Customer)

2 years ago

Yes we use Application Bypass [MSTeams] in our app profile. But it will be applied to ztun2.0.  For ztun1.0, this bypass will not applied.  i totally suspect DNS as reason for this issue.  Its not ZIA that blocks the connection, its ZPA which conflicts and failed to resolve any url into IP. Subsequent traffic is blocked since DNS failed. Whenever i restart service in the Zscaler app, DNS get response as well as MSTeams connects for few seconds.

Gk

(Customer)

2 years ago

i have 2 win11 machine with same ZCC 4.2.0.217. One machine works and another doesn't. i  compared file by file defference in Programfile/Zscaler , Programdata/zscaler in both the machine. In the non working machine dns lookup fails to resolve whereas in working machine dns lookup works. Since the DNS lookup failus, teams cannot communicate. Non working machine started to work, if i exit zscaler app or restarting ZCC service in ZCC-> More -> Restart service.

Something relevant to DNS or network drivers  [may be zpa service] conflicts with windows defender in few machine. these two machine might have difference in update package, or windows version etc.

Does any other company reported similar issue? was it resolved for them.

Gk

(Customer)

2 years ago

## Slow performance resolution requires

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AILajACQT/slow-performance-resolution-requires
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-02-07T11:06:12.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZPA - App Protection

User16757083679091500289

(Customer) asked a question.

February 6, 2024 at 7:00 PM

Slow performance resolution requires

Community, I wanted to pick everyone's brain as I've experienced an issue that has us and support stumped.

We're using ZPA, and had an issue where only Windows clients had very slow performance when access resources. In addition, these were only Windows clients that were on-prem routing through our Private Service Edge. (All users on/off network require Zscaler to access resources) Oddly, Macs that were on-prem weren't impacted.

4.3.0.151

of the client connector and don't have anti-tampering configured. (There's one newer release that addresses a network issue when using anti-tampering) Also, the client was updated a few weeks ago too.

Overall I'm concerned that I don't have a real root cause unless its common practice to have users exist/re-start their ZCC during the workday.

Ben_Garrison

Hello!

The documentation that I can find mentions using some the command line to enable this during installation.  A lot of those images in that article are broken, so I can't tell how Niladri was executing the installation commands. But if you are passing in commands maybe this would help?

For Windows, the command would be something like:

msiexec.exe /i "C:nameof zscalerclientconnectorversionxxx.msi" /qn/l*v

c:\Zcc.txt

CLOUDNAME="examplezscalertwo" STRICTENFORCEMENT=1 USERDOMAIN="

company.com

" POLICYTOKE="ZCCApp portal policy token of the policy used for users"

For macOS, the command would be something like:

sudo sh /System/Volumes/Data/Users/jaysharma/Downloads/Zscaler-osx-3.6.1.27-installer.pkg /Contents/MacOS/

installbuilder.sh

--cloudName zscalertwo --policyToken 123456789 --strictEnforcement

Please replace the placeholders with your actual values.
